metadata.source: HIPAA Security Rule — 45 CFR §164.308–§164.312 (administrative, physical, and technical safeguards for ePHI).
metadata.intendedFor: Covered-entity and business-associate security policy and BAA review for ePHI safeguards.

rules.naturalLanguage: The entity must conduct an accurate and thorough, periodic, documented risk analysis covering all systems handling ePHI. A one-time or single-system assessment is a gap.
rules.lambda: (input1.text.Contains("risk analysis") || input1.text.Contains("risk assessment")) && (input1.text.Contains("annually") || input1.text.Contains("annual") || input1.text.Contains("periodic") || input1.text.Contains("organization-wide") || input1.text.Contains("organisation-wide")) && !(input1.text.Contains("of its primary") || input1.text.Contains("one-time") || input1.text.Contains("in 2024") || input1.text.Contains("in 2025") || input1.text.Contains("in 2023"))
rules.remediation: Update {section.heading} to describe a periodic (e.g., annual) organization-wide documented risk analysis covering every system that creates, receives, maintains, or transmits ePHI, per §164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A).
rules.evidenceQuote: §164.308(a)(1)(ii)(A): Conduct an accurate and thorough assessment of the potential risks and vulnerabilities to the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of all ePHI.

rules.naturalLanguage: The entity must apply sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with security policies. A documented sanction / disciplinary policy must be present.
rules.remediation: Add a {section.heading} sub-clause describing a documented workforce sanction / progressive disciplinary policy with HR tracking, per §164.308(a)(1)(ii)(C).
rules.evidenceQuote: §164.308(a)(1)(ii)(C): Apply appropriate sanctions against workforce members who fail to comply with the security policies and procedures.

rules.naturalLanguage: Access to ePHI must be role-based with documented procedures for granting AND terminating access. Granting access without a termination/deprovisioning procedure is a gap.
rules.remediation: Update {section.heading} to describe role-based access on least privilege AND a documented termination/deprovisioning workflow tied to HR, per §164.308(a)(3)–(a)(4).
rules.evidenceQuote: §164.308(a)(3)–(a)(4): Implement procedures for authorization, supervision, and termination of access to ePHI.

rules.naturalLanguage: The entity must implement recurring security awareness and training for all workforce members. Training only at hire / one-time orientation is a gap.
rules.remediation: Update {section.heading} to require recurring (at least annual) HIPAA security training for all workforce members with periodic phishing/security reminders, per §164.308(a)(5).
rules.evidenceQuote: §164.308(a)(5): Implement a security awareness and training program for all members of the workforce.

rules.naturalLanguage: The entity must address backup, disaster recovery, AND emergency-mode operation. Backups alone are not sufficient.
rules.lambda: (input1.text.Contains("backup") || input1.text.Contains("Backup")) && (input1.text.Contains("disaster recovery") || input1.text.Contains("DR plan") || input1.text.Contains("RTO")) && (input1.text.Contains("emergency-mode") || input1.text.Contains("emergency mode"))
rules.remediation: Expand {section.heading} to cover all three components: data backup plan, disaster recovery plan with defined RTO/RPO, and emergency-mode operation plan, per §164.308(a)(7).
rules.evidenceQuote: §164.308(a)(7): Establish (and implement as needed) policies and procedures for responding to an emergency or other occurrence (data backup plan, disaster recovery plan, emergency mode operation plan).

rules.naturalLanguage: Each user must have a unique identifier; shared or generic accounts on ePHI systems are a gap. Automatic logoff is addressable but should be present or documented as an alternative.
rules.lambda: (input1.text.Contains("unique identifier") || input1.text.Contains("unique user")) && (!input1.text.Contains("shared account") || input1.text.Contains("prohibit")) && (!input1.text.Contains("generic account") || input1.text.Contains("prohibit"))
rules.remediation: Update {section.heading} to enforce unique user identifiers, prohibit shared/generic accounts, and add an automatic logoff (or document a justified alternative), per §164.312(a)(1).
rules.evidenceQuote: §164.312(a)(2)(i): Assign a unique name and/or number for identifying and tracking user identity.
rules.sourceContent: Access Control: Unique User ID & Automatic Logoff (REQUIRED / ADDRESSABLE).

rules.naturalLanguage: The entity must implement audit logging on ePHI systems with periodic review. Logs collected but never reviewed is a gap.
rules.lambda: (input1.text.Contains("audit log") || input1.text.Contains("audit logs") || input1.text.Contains("audit logging")) && (input1.text.Contains("reviewed") || input1.text.Contains("review") || input1.text.Contains("alerting"))
rules.remediation: Update {section.heading} to require audit logging on every system containing ePHI AND a periodic review (e.g., weekly) with alerting on anomalies, per §164.312(b).
rules.evidenceQuote: §164.312(b): Implement hardware, software, and/or procedural mechanisms that record and examine activity in information systems that contain or use ePHI.

rules.naturalLanguage: ePHI must be encrypted in transit (TLS 1.2+) AND at rest (e.g., AES-256), or a documented equivalent measure. Encryption in transit only with PHI unencrypted at rest is a gap.
rules.lambda: (input1.text.Contains("TLS 1.2") || input1.text.Contains("TLS 1.3")) && (input1.text.Contains("AES-256") || input1.text.Contains("encrypted at rest") || input1.text.Contains("at rest using"))
rules.remediation: Update {section.heading} to commit to TLS 1.2+ in transit AND AES-256 (or equivalent CSE-approved) encryption at rest for all ePHI, per §164.312(e).
rules.evidenceQuote: §164.312(e): Implement technical security measures to guard against unauthorized access to ePHI transmitted over an electronic communications network.
